features: THE CREDIT THAT GREW WHILE YOU SPENT IT — No migration: the database is not touched. Two defects on the same subject, one visible and one not, which had to be fixed together.

THE CREDIT NOTE COULD NOT BE USED. The accounting engine has always known how to offset: given a properly built payment, the invoice closes and the books balance even when not a euro leaves the bank. But the payment screen did not know how to build one — and that same screen had a button offering to offset automatically with one click. Pressing it always ended in «imbalance detected between debit and credit», and the payment was not saved. This was not an edge case: it was every use of a credit note from that screen, including selecting it by hand.

WHY IT HAPPENED: an invoice partly covered by credit must appear twice in the entry — one line for the part leaving the bank and one for the part offset — and the screen wrote only one. The correct shape had been specified since 2025 and the engine already implemented it; it was the interface that did not. The calculation now lives in a module of its own, covered by nineteen automated checks that verify the balance case by case, before anything is sent.

UNDERNEATH THERE WAS A SECOND ONE, HIDDEN BY THE FIRST. The remaining credit on a note was calculated backwards: a note worth € 2,440.00, after € 1,220.00 had been offset, reported € 3,660.00 still available. The credit grew as you spent it, and the guard that prevents over-consumption read that inflated figure. Fixing only the button would have turned a visible error into three invoices marked «paid» with € 1,220.00 of invented credit and no money leaving the bank — which is why both were fixed together.

THE SCREEN NOW SAYS WHAT IT IS ABOUT TO DO, BEFORE DOING IT. The amber panel was called «Smart Router — Netting 1-Click» and the button «Offset automatically»: two names that tell a building manager neither what is there nor what happens on pressing. The panel now says the supplier has credit notes available, and underneath it says what the button will do — which invoices it touches, in what order, and that nothing is recorded until you confirm. The abbreviations are gone too.

AND IT SAYS HOW MUCH CREDIT CANNOT BE USED. If the note is worth more than the selected invoices, the excess cannot be used in that payment: it stays on the note, and this is now stated rather than inferred from the totals. The panel listing what will be written to the books was also corrected: it said «Payment» on lines that were offsets — showing something different from what was being sent.

A FULL GUIDE AT THE TOP OF THE PAGE, as on other screens. This page does five things that cannot be deduced from their names — offsetting, checking the IBAN against the supplier record, flagging a suspected duplicate payment within twenty-four hours, account balance sufficiency, and the legal cash limit — and none of them was explained anywhere.

UNDER THE BONNET: nine new checks on the accounting side and nineteen on the offset calculation, including one that replays the whole scenario — three invoices and one note, the first two offsets accepted and the third refused — and one that verifies the old payload really is rejected, so the defect cannot return silently. Five error messages that placed the euro symbol after the amount were also corrected, along with the page layout on narrow screens.
